messages.subject: SUBJECT_NESTED
parts:
Hi

I get different number of unique runs in my original file that I feed into the MSStats than what I get out after log2 -and normalisation. This is because when group number is the same (for instance 4) and the subject is 1 or 10, then the subject_nested is 4.1 in both cases.

Is this a problem?

messages.author: df9ba0266a9a081f
messages.subject: Re: SUBJECT_NESTED
parts:
Hi Petri,

The unique runs is not related with Subject_nested column during the process. and If I understood correctly, subject_nested column also seems wrong. It should be 4.1 and 4.10. I suspected the class of columns in the data seems wrong. However, It will be good for me to check it and confirm what the problem is in order to prevent the same problem for other users. Could you share msstats.log file and any partial data you used (at least one protein data)? 
Thank you.

-Meena

messages.author: df9ba0266a9a081f
messages.subject: Re: SUBJECT_NESTED
parts:
Dear Users,

First of all, Thank you Petri for addressing this issue.

We found that this issue came from csv file. If you save the output('ProcessedData') of 'dataProcess' function as csv file, 4.1 and 4.10 become as the same 4.10 (numeric value) in the example above. However, 'Run' column still distinguish 4.1 and 4.10 as different number. If you didn't save it as csv file and re-read it, which means just use 'dataProcess' and use 'groupComparion' with the output of 'dataProcess', there is no problem at all. You can check the correct SUBJECT_NESTED and RUN column information with the command lines below,

quant<-dataProcess(raw)
quantprocess<-quant$ProcessedData
unique(quantprocess[,c("SUBJECT","SUBJECT_NESTED","RUN")]

However, we will change the way to assign SUBJECT_NESTED column in order to prevent this confusion.
Thank you.

-Meena
